subject: Urban Planning
title: Detroit's Decline: When the City Lost Its Purpose
description: A quick, practical guide to Detroit's Decline: When the City Lost Its Purpose.

hook.text: Detroit went from 1.8 million people in 1950 to 640,000 by 2020. A third of the city is now vacant land.

buildup.text: Auto companies built suburban factories. White residents followed on new highways. The tax base collapsed.

discovery.text: The city demolished 27,000 abandoned homes since 2014. Entire blocks have returned to empty grassland.

twist.text: Detroit filed for bankruptcy in 2013 — the largest municipal bankruptcy in US history at $18 billion.

climax.text: Urban farming, downtown revival, and tech investment are slowly rebuilding, but for a much smaller population.

punchline.text: The Motor City was built by cars. Then cars drove everyone away.

quiz.question: How much of Detroit's population did it lose between 1950 and 2020?
